note: Zapier exposes no public import format for arbitrary Zaps — Zap definitions are not portable artifacts the way n8n workflow JSON is. These are BUILD INSTRUCTIONS for the Zapier editor; the portability asymmetry is finding F-1 in FINDINGS.md.
scenarios: Release 1 (09_ §2). The Release-2 call-review and email-triage scenarios are parked, not deleted — see 09_ §1.
status: NOT BUILT — no Zapier account exists in the Builder environment

every_http_step_must_send.X-Provider-Key: the provider credential the stub prints at startup (no owner authority; distinct from the owner key)
every_http_step_must_send.Content-Type: application/json — the stub refuses anything else (SEC-R1-08)

zaps.name: Builder-return pipeline

steps.config: Apply the envelope AND bind the five-component identity tuple: task_id, transition, artifact_digest (COMPUTED here from the artifact, never taken from the sender), target_role (symbolic), submission_epoch. Record artifact_bytes and manifest_file_count for the R1P-05 artifact-handling measures
steps.boundary: C-1 — a raw archive hash alone is not identity
returns a resume token, OR duplicate-suppressed with the prior receipt (R1P-04 test 1), OR rejected-unauthorized-target (test 3)
duplicate suppression and target rejection must NOT read as success

steps.app: Human in the Loop by Zapier
steps.config: Carries the pause only. The card and the decision live on the AI OS surface; Zapier never learns the case id
steps.boundary: packet §3 — the provider may carry the pause, never decide it
the endpoint is an allowlist; any additional field is refused

steps.config: POST to action_request.endpoint with {capability, action_request_id, case_id, payload} exactly as returned
steps.boundary: C-2/C-3 — the destination comes from the ActionRequest the AI OS built by resolving the ROLE; the capability is single-use and bound to the payload digest. A replay returns the prior receipt with an explicit no-second-side-effect marker (R1P-04 test 4)

steps.config: AI OS /poc1/receipt with the raw provider result

measures: unauthorized-target rejection distinguishable from duplicate success
r1p05_artifact_measures: binary fidelity and digest preservation end to end
behaviour on nested archives, symlinks, traversal paths and malformed archives (failing closed is a recordable capability gap, not a POC failure)
whether the provider stores, inspects or retains artifact contents
owner-card latency without the artifact entering Discord

zaps.name: Idea capture and staging

steps.config: Separate Case A (authenticated owner-authored: owner instruction authority) from Case B (imported/forwarded: external-untrusted, instruction authority NONE). Embedded external content inside a Case A idea keeps its own class
steps.boundary: R1P-02 — owner authorship and external content are two trust cases and must not share one class

steps.config: AI OS /poc2/triage — new-topic vs existing-project-addition, staged record, and the instruction-authority verdict
steps.boundary: the AI OS classifies; Zapier transports
the POC's proof obligation: external content informs classification WITHOUT acquiring instruction authority

explicitly_absent: no send step of any kind
measures: trust isolation across the two cases

zaps.name: Durable nightly integrity sweep

steps.boundary: the provider hosts the schedule; the AI OS journal owns the spec

steps.config: AI OS /poc3/run-started declaring schedule_id and occurrence, and passing the Zap run id as provider_correlation_id
steps.boundary: C-13 — the run id is MINTED BY THE AI OS. A duplicate declaration is refused 409 and preserves the prior record, which is what makes the mid-flight kill measurable

steps.config: POST to the returned stage_endpoint with {run_id}; leave Zapier's autoreplay/retry enabled
steps.boundary: C-4 — retry-tolerant by design; a single-use rule here would fail the round's own mandated kill

steps.config: side_effect_certain is true; otherwise branch to /poc3/reconcile
steps.boundary: ACT-01 — uncertain outcomes reconcile rather than re-fire

zaps.induced_failure_required: kill the run mid-flight between the stage and the checkpoint and record the ACTUAL retry/replay behaviour — packet §4 forbids simulating this in prose. The stub's 409-on-duplicate-declaration preserves the prior run record so 'resumed' and 'replayed from the top' are distinguishable, which they were not in R1
measures: stage attempts recorded separately from deliveries
